title: Is asking AI how to code somehow vibe coding?
author: kofkof78
selftext:
Silly question it might be but if I'm using AI to tell me how to use blueprints in UE to make my game, is it considered as vibe coding?

The definition seems to be blury to me.

I am working this way to learn what I'm doing if there is any problem. Basically I'm asking AI how to make this or that and it explains to me and I go back & forth with it. It probably takes way more time than asking directly the AI to code for me but I prefere this way.

Thanks in advance.

comments.author: Ohgood9002
comments.body:
Why do you even care? Use your tools however you want and make whatever you want. The only people that care are those who are too stubborn to pivot to new technologies.

Fuck em. No one can dictate how you create.

replies.author: kofkof78
replies.body: I want to see ai as a colleague/tutor, not a subordinate. If it makes any sense

comments.author: proto-cool
comments.body: As you described it, I don't think so, no. You're still making the judgment call on whether or not that Blueprint block is of any benefit to your project or not.

comments.author: SentientDreamer
comments.body: No. Asking it questions and learning isn't vibe coding. Vibe coding is the practice of using AI as a middleman in order to code in plain English.

comments.author: _DCtheTall_
comments.body:
No, I do not consider that vibe coding. Vibe coding is when you just let the AI do the coding for you as a black box.

What you are doing is AI-assisted coding, and it is a good thing to practice to keep up your writing skills. I also recommend having AI review your code as well and then applying the fixes yourself, very educational.

comments.author: Heavy_Extent_3863
comments.body:
1. Blueprints are dead 
2. You are just wasting time you rather should spend with game design

comments.author: MaksRengi
comments.body: If you know why your blueprint works its not vibe coding. Vibe coding is when it works somehow and youre scared to touch it

comments.author: OkMorning420
comments.body: Blueprints is going away for AI assisted Verse so I wouldn't spend too much time focusing on Blueprints.

comments.author: Maleficent-Path5590
comments.body:
No one gives a fuck, go code it with AI

The average customer only cares about the end product, not about the steps taken to get there.

comments.author: LearningCrochet
comments.body: i wouldnt consider it so. Vibe coding is just coding based off vibes but if you understand the intent and the how it'll make things easier down the road than hitting your head on the same obstacle 10 hours in

comments.author: Long-Staff8758
comments.body: Honestly, letting the AI do end-to-end product development (ideation, design, system design, development) is vibe coding

comments.author: TheAmazingElys
comments.body:
My definition of vibecoding: Asking AI to code without looking too much at the code. You can vibecode a function, a class, an entire package or even a product.

If you have the ownership of every line of code, it's mostly autocomplete on steroid.

comments.author: GornoUmaethiVrurzu
comments.body: Vibe coding is when you tell it to code and you don't code yourself. You're using it as a tutor

comments.author: Aeropar
comments.body:
No I don’t think so, but there’s also nothing wrong with Vibe Coding, if you need / if it suits your project, have it draft some functionality, inspect it and ask it questions of how things work, then you learn how the code works and from their you can guide it with more educated decisions, that way the whole thing works in the way you intend it to, rather than just relying on it to get it right without your direction. How can you ensure it stays on the road if you don’t know how to drive?

That’s basically my point :)

comments.author: Monecreiff
comments.body: no thats an American teacher. You learn by reading what they spew out at you

comments.author: Brettinabox
comments.body: Followup question, does assisted coding and/or using ai as a tutor need a disclaimer?

replies.author: kofkof78
replies.body: Really good question. I'll probably ask steam once I'm ready to show my game (next year I assume)

replies.author: Brettinabox
replies.body: i think one of the bigger improvements ive made is also asking ai in a roundabout way how professional game devs operate, then incorporating that workflow into the process

comments.author: kiwibonga
comments.body: You have caught the vibe cooties, now you're just one step away from vibe AIDS.

comments.author: emptybottlesss
comments.body: Asking ai questions is no different than going into a text book and looking for the answer. No that's not what vibe coding means. It means to directly prompt the ai. But just understand people mostly care about art when it comes to Ai. That's normally when you'll hear words like Ai slop.
